etymology: Hebrew goel (גֹּאֵל) — "redeemer, kinsman with right to redeem."
biblical_def: The Old Testament office of kinsman-redeemer — a near relative who buys back lost property, marries the widow, or avenges blood (Lev 25:25; Deut 25:5; Num 35); fulfilled in Christ.
webster_summary: The kinsman-redeemer of the Old Testament law.
webster_full: The Old Testament office and right of a near kinsman to redeem family land that has been sold off, to marry a brother's childless widow (levirate marriage), or to avenge blood — all aspects of preserving the covenant family. Christ is the goel of His people.
scriptures: Leviticus 25:25
If thy brother be waxen poor, and hath sold away some of his possession, and if any of his kin come to redeem it, then shall he redeem that which his brother sold.
Ruth 4:14
Blessed be the LORD, which hath not left thee this day without a kinsman, that his name may be famous in Israel.
For I know that my redeemer liveth, and that he shall stand at the latter day upon the earth.
corruption_summary: Reduced to ancient legal curiosity, missing how thoroughly the office foreshadows Christ.
corruption_paragraphs: Goel is the gospel in advance. Boaz redeems Ruth; Christ redeems His bride. The kinsman with right to redeem must be both able and willing — Christ alone fits both. Read Ruth as Christology.
usage: Christ is our goel — kinsman, able, willing.
Read Ruth and Job 19 together for goel theology.

etymology: From Latin levir "husband's brother."
biblical_def: The Old Testament law (Deut 25:5-10) requiring a man to marry his brother's childless widow to raise up offspring in the dead brother's name; basis for the Ruth-Boaz story and the Sadducees' question to Jesus.
webster_summary: Marriage to a brother's childless widow.
webster_full: The Mosaic law commanding a man to marry the widow of his deceased brother who died childless, that the firstborn might bear the dead brother's name and inherit his property — preserving the family line and inheritance.
scriptures: Deuteronomy 25:5
If brethren dwell together, and one of them die, and have no child... her husband's brother shall go in unto her, and take her to him to wife.
Genesis 38:8
And Judah said unto Onan, Go in unto thy brother's wife, and marry her, and raise up seed to thy brother.
Matthew 22:24-28
Master, Moses said, If a man die, having no children, his brother shall marry his wife, and raise up seed unto his brother.
corruption_summary: Read as ancient peculiarity, missing how it preserved family inheritance and pointed to gospel-themes of seed and widow.
corruption_paragraphs: Levirate marriage is not random — it preserves the dead brother's name, his land, and his line. Tamar fights for it; Onan refuses it; Boaz fulfills it; the Sadducees use it to attack the resurrection. Trace the thread.
usage: Levirate marriage preserved name and land.
Boaz fulfilled what Onan refused.

etymology: Hebrew Urim ve-Tummim (אוּרִים וְתֻמִּים) — "lights and perfections."
biblical_def: The mysterious objects placed in the high priest's breastplate by which God communicated decisions to Israel before the era of established prophets (Exod 28:30; 1 Sam 28:6).
webster_summary: Priestly objects for divine guidance.
webster_full: The mysterious objects God commanded to be placed in the high priest's breastplate of judgment by which divine decisions could be inquired in matters affecting Israel; their precise nature is unknown but their use is biblically attested.
scriptures: Exodus 28:30
And thou shalt put in the breastplate of judgment the Urim and the Thummim; and they shall be upon Aaron's heart, when he goeth in before the LORD.
Numbers 27:21
He shall stand before Eleazar the priest, who shall ask counsel for him after the judgment of Urim before the LORD.
1 Samuel 28:6
And when Saul enquired of the LORD, the LORD answered him not, neither by dreams, nor by Urim, nor by prophets.
corruption_summary: Treated as magic dice or curiosity; missing the orderly priestly inquiry it embodies.
corruption_paragraphs: Urim and Thummim were not magic. They were the appointed mode of priestly inquiry until prophets and the written Word displaced them. The lesson is that God provides means of guidance suited to His people's stage in revelation.
usage: God gave Urim before He gave the prophets.
Lights and perfections in the priestly breastplate.

etymology: Hebrew amud esh — pillar of fire.
biblical_def: The visible nighttime presence of YHWH leading Israel through the wilderness — by night a pillar of fire, by day a pillar of cloud (Exod 13:21-22; Num 9:15-23).
webster_summary: YHWH's nighttime presence with Israel.
webster_full: The pillar of fire by which YHWH visibly led, illumined, and protected Israel during their wilderness night-marches; complement to the pillar of cloud by day; sign of divine presence and guidance.
scriptures: Exodus 13:21
And the LORD went before them by day in a pillar of a cloud, to lead them the way; and by night in a pillar of fire, to give them light.
Exodus 14:24
It came to pass, that in the morning watch the LORD looked unto the host of the Egyptians through the pillar of fire.
Nehemiah 9:12
Moreover thou leddest them in the day by a cloudy pillar; and in the night by a pillar of fire.
corruption_summary: Reduced to a Sunday-school illustration, missing the theological depth of God's tangible presence in the wilderness.
corruption_paragraphs: The pillar of fire was God Himself dwelling visibly with His people — a forerunner of the indwelling Spirit. The God who gave a pillar of fire then gave tongues of fire at Pentecost. The same God; the same gracious presence.
roots_summary: Hebrew amud esh — pillar of fire.
usage: The pillar of fire prefigures Pentecost.
God's presence guides through the night.

etymology: Hebrew terumah (תְּרוּמָה) — "contribution lifted up."
biblical_def: An offering portion lifted up and set apart for God's use, often becoming the priests' food allotment (Num 18:8-32; Exod 29:27).
webster_summary: An offering lifted up and set apart for the priests.
webster_full: A specific category of Mosaic offering in which a portion was lifted (heaved) toward the LORD, then given to the priests as their share for sustenance — a tangible witness that the priests served at the people's expense.
scriptures: Exodus 29:27
And thou shalt sanctify the breast of the wave offering, and the shoulder of the heave offering, which is waved, and which is heaved up.
Numbers 18:24
But the tithes of the children of Israel, which they offer as an heave offering unto the LORD, I have given to the Levites.
Leviticus 7:32
And the right shoulder shall ye give unto the priest for an heave offering.
corruption_summary: Forgotten as obsolete ritual; missing how it visibly portrayed the people's support of priestly ministry.
corruption_paragraphs: The heave offering teaches a permanent principle: those who serve at the altar live by the altar. Pastoral support is not optional under the new covenant either. Paul argues from heave-offering to gospel-support directly (1 Cor 9:13-14).
roots_summary: Hebrew terumah — that which is lifted up.
usage: Support those who serve at the altar.
The heave offering teaches gospel-support.

etymology: Hebrew asham (אָשָׁם) — "guilt offering."
biblical_def: The Mosaic offering for specific sins involving violation of property or sacred things, requiring restitution plus a fifth (Lev 5:14-19; 6:1-7); also called the guilt offering.
webster_summary: The guilt offering with restitution.
webster_full: The Mosaic sacrifice for specific transgressions involving the property of God or neighbor — sacrilege, fraud, theft, false oaths — requiring not only sacrifice but full restitution plus a one-fifth penalty paid to the wronged party.
scriptures: Leviticus 6:5
He shall even restore it in the principal, and shall add the fifth part more thereto.
Leviticus 7:1
Likewise this is the law of the trespass offering: it is most holy.
Isaiah 53:10
When thou shalt make his soul an offering for sin (asham)...
corruption_summary: Reduced to dispensational trivia; missing how it required real-world restitution and how Isaiah names the Servant as asham.
corruption_paragraphs: The trespass offering had teeth — sacrifice plus restitution plus a fifth. Forgiveness did not erase what you owed your neighbor. And Isaiah 53:10 names the Suffering Servant as asham — Christ as our trespass offering, paying both God and the wronged.
usage: Christ is our asham; we still owe restitution to neighbor.
Forgiven sin still has earthly consequences.

etymology: Hebrew minchah (מִנְחָה) — "gift, present, grain offering."
biblical_def: The grain offering of fine flour, oil, and frankincense, often accompanying animal sacrifices; signified consecrated labor and dedication (Lev 2; Num 28).
webster_summary: The grain offering of fine flour and oil.
webster_full: The Mosaic grain offering of fine flour, mixed with oil and frankincense, sometimes baked and sometimes raw; never with leaven or honey; presented either alone or in conjunction with animal sacrifices to consecrate the fruit of human labor.
scriptures: Leviticus 2:1
When any will offer a meat offering unto the LORD, his offering shall be of fine flour; and he shall pour oil upon it, and put frankincense thereon.
Leviticus 2:11
No meat offering... shall be made with leaven: for ye shall burn no leaven, nor any honey, in any offering.
Numbers 28:5
And a tenth part of an ephah of flour for a meat offering, mingled with the fourth part of an hin of beaten oil.
corruption_summary: Confused with English 'meat' (KJV uses 'meat offering' for the grain offering); modern speakers miss it is grain, not meat.
corruption_paragraphs: Older English uses 'meat' for any food (cf. 'meat in due season'). The minchah is the grain offering — the fruit of human labor consecrated to God. It teaches that work-product itself is offering: bread and oil, not just blood and animal.
usage: Consecrate your labor as meal-offering.
Bread and oil also are sacrifice.

etymology: Hebrew Yom Kippur (יוֹם כִּפּוּר) — Day of Covering.
biblical_def: The annual high holy day on the tenth of the seventh month when the high priest entered the Holy of Holies with sacrificial blood for the sins of the nation (Lev 16; Heb 9-10).
webster_summary: Israel's annual day of national atonement.
webster_full: The annual day on the tenth of the seventh month (Tishri) when the high priest, after elaborate purifications, entered the Holy of Holies with the blood of bull and goat to make atonement for himself and the people; the scapegoat carried away their sins.
scriptures: Leviticus 16:30
For on that day shall the priest make an atonement for you, to cleanse you, that ye may be clean from all your sins before the LORD.
Hebrews 9:7
But into the second went the high priest alone once every year, not without blood.
Hebrews 9:12
By his own blood he entered in once into the holy place, having obtained eternal redemption for us.
corruption_summary: Treated as ancient ritual; missing how Hebrews makes it the controlling type for Christ's once-for-all atonement.
corruption_paragraphs: Yom Kippur happens annually because it is provisional. Hebrews argues: every annual repetition proves the sacrifices cannot finally remove sin. Christ enters once, with His own blood, into the true Holy of Holies, and obtains eternal redemption.
usage: Yom Kippur points to Christ's once-for-all atonement.
Read Leviticus 16 alongside Hebrews 9-10.

etymology: Hebrew menorah (מְנוֹרָה) — the seven-branched golden candelabrum.
biblical_def: The seven-branched golden candelabrum in the Holy Place of tabernacle and temple, fed continually with pure olive oil; the only light in the holy place (Exod 25:31-40; 27:20-21).
webster_summary: The seven-branched lamp of the holy place.
webster_full: The seven-branched golden candelabrum hammered from one piece, standing in the Holy Place of the tabernacle and temple; fed continually with pure olive oil by the priests; the sole light in the holy chamber.
scriptures: Exodus 25:31
And thou shalt make a candlestick of pure gold: of beaten work shall the candlestick be made: his shaft, and his branches, his bowls, his knops, and his flowers, shall be of the same.
Zechariah 4:2-3
Behold a candlestick all of gold, with a bowl upon the top of it, and his seven lamps thereon... and two olive trees by it.
Revelation 1:12-13
Being turned, I saw seven golden candlesticks; and in the midst of the seven candlesticks one like unto the Son of man.
corruption_summary: Forgotten as ritual artifact; missing how it points to Christ as the light and to the Spirit's oil.
corruption_paragraphs: The lampstand fed by olive oil prefigures the Church (the seven candlesticks) lit by the oil of the Spirit. Zechariah 4 makes the connection explicit. Revelation 1 places Christ in the midst of the lampstands. Read the symbolism.
usage: The Church is lampstand; the Spirit is oil; Christ is light.
Read Zechariah 4 for the typology.

etymology: Hebrew mizbeach ha-qetoreth — altar of incense.
biblical_def: The smaller golden altar in the Holy Place where pure incense was burned morning and evening before the veil of the Holy of Holies; symbol of the prayers of the saints (Exod 30:1-10; Rev 8:3-4).
webster_summary: The golden incense altar before the veil.
webster_full: The smaller golden altar standing before the veil in the Holy Place; site of the morning and evening incense burned by the priests; symbol of the prayers of the saints rising before God's throne.
scriptures: Exodus 30:7-8
And Aaron shall burn thereon sweet incense every morning... and at even, he shall burn incense upon it, a perpetual incense before the LORD.
Psalm 141:2
Let my prayer be set forth before thee as incense; and the lifting up of my hands as the evening sacrifice.
Revelation 8:3-4
And another angel came... having a golden censer; and there was given unto him much incense, that he should offer it with the prayers of all saints.
corruption_summary: Reduced to ancient detail; missing how Scripture makes it the symbol of prayer rising before God.
corruption_paragraphs: Pure incense at morning and evening — perpetual prayer before the veil. Psalm 141 owns the typology directly: let my prayer be incense. Revelation completes it: the prayers of the saints rise as incense from the heavenly altar.
usage: Pray morning and evening as incense.
Your prayers reach the heavenly altar.

etymology: Hebrew kiyor (כִּיּוֹר) — basin; bronze made from women's mirrors (Exod 38:8).
biblical_def: The bronze washing basin in the tabernacle court between the bronze altar and the holy place; for the priests' ceremonial washing of hands and feet before service (Exod 30:17-21).
webster_summary: Bronze basin for priestly washing.
webster_full: The bronze basin in the tabernacle court between the bronze altar of sacrifice and the entrance to the Holy Place, where priests washed hands and feet before ministering — a symbol of the cleansing required for service before God.
scriptures: Exodus 30:18-21

Thou shalt also make a laver of brass... and Aaron and his sons shall wash their hands and their feet thereat: when they go into the tabernacle of the congregation, they shall wash with water, that they die not.
Exodus 38:8
And he made the laver of brass, and the foot of it of brass, of the looking glasses of the women assembling.
John 13:8
If I wash thee not, thou hast no part with me.
corruption_summary: Forgotten as ritual furnishings; missing how Christ takes up its function in foot-washing and how the Word washes the church (Eph 5:26).
corruption_paragraphs: Priests had to be washed before service. Christ stoops at the Last Supper to wash His disciples' feet — fulfilling the laver in Person. Ephesians 5 describes the Word as the washing of water that sanctifies the church. The bronze laver theology runs deep.
usage: Be washed before service.
Christ Himself is our laver.

etymology: Hebrew nazir (נָזִיר) — "set apart, consecrated."
biblical_def: The voluntary vow of separation to YHWH described in Numbers 6 — abstaining from wine and grape products, leaving hair uncut, and avoiding contact with the dead.
webster_summary: A vow of voluntary set-apart consecration.
webster_full: A voluntary, time-bounded vow of consecration to YHWH described in Numbers 6, marked by abstention from wine and all grape products, uncut hair, and ritual separation from contact with the dead. Lifelong Nazirites included Samson and Samuel; Paul took a temporary one.
scriptures: Numbers 6:2
When either man or woman shall separate themselves to vow a vow of a Nazarite, to separate themselves unto the LORD.
Judges 13:5
The child shall be a Nazarite unto God from the womb: and he shall begin to deliver Israel out of the hand of the Philistines.
Acts 18:18
Paul... having shorn his head in Cenchrea: for he had a vow.
corruption_summary: Confused with 'Nazarene' (resident of Nazareth); missing the depth of voluntary consecration the vow signifies.
corruption_paragraphs: Nazirite ≠ Nazarene. The Nazirite was anyone who vowed separation. Samson, Samuel, John the Baptist, and Paul (briefly) all took the vow. The principle survives: voluntary times of intensified consecration are part of biblical spirituality.
usage: Take seasons of intensified consecration.
Distinguish Nazirite from Nazarene.

etymology: Hebrew seder (סֵדֶר) — "order," the ritual order of the Passover meal.
biblical_def: The ordered Passover meal commanded in Exodus 12, retold annually with bitter herbs, unleavened bread, lamb, and four cups; the meal Jesus reframed at the Last Supper.
webster_summary: The ordered Passover meal.
webster_full: The ordered ritual Passover meal traced to Exodus 12 — bitter herbs, unleavened bread, roast lamb, four cups of wine — retelling the deliverance from Egypt and forming the framework of the Last Supper that Jesus transformed into the Lord's Supper.
scriptures: Exodus 12:14
And this day shall be unto you for a memorial; and ye shall keep it a feast to the LORD throughout your generations.
With desire I have desired to eat this passover with you before I suffer: For I say unto you, I will not any more eat thereof, until it be fulfilled in the kingdom of God.
1 Corinthians 5:7
For even Christ our passover is sacrificed for us.
corruption_summary: Christianized away from its Jewish roots, losing the rich typology that ties the Last Supper to Exodus.
corruption_paragraphs: The Lord's Supper is a transformed seder. The four cups, the unleavened bread, the bitter herbs — Jesus uses each to declare Himself the true Passover. To lose the seder background is to lose half the meaning of communion.
usage: Read the seder to deepen the Lord's Supper.
Christ our Passover is sacrificed for us.

etymology: Hebrew Shavuot (שָׁבוּעוֹת) — "weeks"; Greek Pentekostē — fiftieth (day).
biblical_def: The annual feast seven weeks (50 days) after Passover, celebrating the wheat harvest's first fruits; the day on which the Spirit was poured out at Pentecost (Lev 23:15-22; Acts 2).
webster_summary: Pentecost; harvest-feast 50 days after Passover.
webster_full: The annual harvest feast falling fifty days (seven weeks plus a day) after Passover, celebrating the wheat firstfruits with two leavened loaves; the Greek-named Pentecost; the day of the Spirit's outpouring on the church.
scriptures: Leviticus 23:15-16
And ye shall count unto you from the morrow after the sabbath... seven sabbaths shall be complete: even unto the morrow after the seventh sabbath shall ye number fifty days.
Deuteronomy 16:10
Thou shalt keep the feast of weeks unto the LORD thy God.
Acts 2:1
And when the day of Pentecost was fully come, they were all with one accord in one place.
corruption_summary: Christianized as 'Pentecost' detached from its harvest meaning, missing the firstfruits-of-Spirit theology.
corruption_paragraphs: Pentecost is the firstfruits-of-the-Spirit harvest. Christ rose at firstfruits of grain (Passover); the Spirit comes at firstfruits of wheat (Weeks). The feast calendar prophesies the gospel calendar. Acts 2 is not random timing.
usage: Pentecost completes the firstfruits cycle.
Read Acts 2 alongside Leviticus 23.

etymology: Hebrew Yom Teruah (יוֹם תְּרוּעָה) — "day of trumpet blast"; later Rosh Hashanah.
biblical_def: The first day of the seventh month, marked by the blowing of trumpets (shofar); a sabbath rest and holy convocation, opening the high holy days (Lev 23:23-25; Num 29:1-6).
webster_summary: The trumpet-blast feast opening the seventh month.
webster_full: The annual feast on the first day of the seventh month (Tishri) marked by the blowing of trumpets (shofar) — a sabbath rest and holy convocation that opened the climactic high holy days leading to Yom Kippur and Tabernacles. Later named Rosh Hashanah.
scriptures: Leviticus 23:24
In the seventh month, in the first day of the month, shall ye have a sabbath, a memorial of blowing of trumpets, an holy convocation.
Numbers 29:1
In the seventh month, on the first day of the month, ye shall have an holy convocation; ye shall do no servile work: it is a day of blowing the trumpets unto you.
1 Thessalonians 4:16
For the Lord himself shall descend from heaven with a shout, with the voice of the archangel, and with the trump of God.
corruption_summary: Forgotten in most Christian calendars; missing the eschatological trumpet-imagery that runs from Sinai to the Last Trump.
corruption_paragraphs: The shofar runs through Scripture: Sinai's trumpet, jubilee's trumpet, the trumpet that rallies armies, the seven trumpets of Revelation, and the last trump that gathers the saints. Yom Teruah keeps the trumpet awake.
usage: The trumpet calls to assembly and battle and feast.
The last trump will yet sound.

etymology: Hebrew arei miqlat — cities of asylum.
biblical_def: Six Levitical cities (three east of Jordan, three west) appointed to shelter manslayers from the avenger of blood until trial and the high priest's death (Num 35; Josh 20).
webster_summary: Six asylum cities for accidental manslayers.
webster_full: Six Levitical cities — three east of the Jordan (Bezer, Ramoth, Golan), three west (Kedesh, Shechem, Hebron) — appointed to provide asylum for those who killed accidentally, sheltering them from the avenger of blood until standing trial and remaining until the high priest's death.
scriptures: Numbers 35:11-12
Then ye shall appoint you cities to be cities of refuge for you; that the slayer may flee thither, which killeth any person at unawares.
Joshua 20:7-8
And they appointed Kedesh in Galilee... and Shechem... and Kirjatharba, which is Hebron... and Bezer... and Ramoth... and Golan.
Hebrews 6:18
Who have fled for refuge to lay hold upon the hope set before us.
corruption_summary: Forgotten as obscure; missing how Hebrews 6:18 makes Christ Himself our city of refuge.
corruption_paragraphs: The cities of refuge taught a profound truth: there is a place where the avenger cannot reach. Hebrews 6:18 picks it up directly — we have fled for refuge in Christ. The high priest's death released the manslayer; the High Priest's death releases us.
roots_summary: Hebrew arei miqlat — cities of refuge.
usage: Christ is our city of refuge.
The High Priest's death releases.

etymology: Hebrew goel ha-dam — redeemer of blood.
biblical_def: The nearest male relative of a slain person, charged with executing justice on the killer; bounded by Mosaic law through the cities of refuge to limit private vengeance (Num 35:19-27).
webster_summary: The kinsman who exacts justice for shed blood.
webster_full: The nearest male relative of a slain person, charged in Mosaic law with executing justice on the killer; the cities of refuge bounded his pursuit to prevent unjust killing of accidental manslayers.
scriptures: Numbers 35:19
The revenger of blood himself shall slay the murderer: when he meeteth him, he shall slay him.
Deuteronomy 19:6
Lest the avenger of the blood pursue the slayer, while his heart is hot.
Joshua 20:5
And if the avenger of blood pursue after him, then they shall not deliver the slayer up into his hand.
corruption_summary: Read as primitive vengeance, missing how Mosaic law actually constrained and ordered blood-justice.
corruption_paragraphs: Mosaic law did not invent blood-vengeance — it constrained and ordered it. Cities of refuge protected the accidental killer; assemblies tried cases; the avenger could not arbitrarily kill. The system replaced clan warfare with covenant justice.
roots_summary: Hebrew goel ha-dam — redeemer of blood.
usage: The avenger of blood was bounded by law.
Justice without limit becomes injustice.

etymology: Hebrew qarnoth ha-mizbeach — horns of the altar.
biblical_def: The four upraised projections at the corners of the bronze and golden altars; sites where sacrificial blood was applied and to which fugitives clung as last refuge (Exod 27:2; 1 Kings 1:50-51; 2:28).
webster_summary: The four corner-projections of the altar; place of refuge.
webster_full: The four upraised projections at the corners of the tabernacle altars where sacrificial blood was applied; also where fugitives clung as a final plea for mercy. Adonijah and Joab both fled to them in the early monarchy.
scriptures: Exodus 27:2
And thou shalt make the horns of it upon the four corners thereof: his horns shall be of the same.
1 Kings 1:50
And Adonijah feared because of Solomon, and arose, and went, and caught hold on the horns of the altar.
1 Kings 2:28
Then tidings came to Joab... and Joab fled unto the tabernacle of the LORD, and caught hold on the horns of the altar.
corruption_summary: Forgotten architectural detail; missing the rich symbolism of horn-as-strength and altar-as-refuge.
corruption_paragraphs: Horns in Scripture symbolize strength; the altar's horns make the place of sacrifice the place of strongest refuge. Adonijah and Joab both fled there. The image teaches: the place where blood was shed is the place where mercy is found.
usage: Cling to the horns of the altar.
The cross is the horn of mercy.

etymology: Hebrew mizbeach ha-nechosheth — altar of bronze.
biblical_def: The large square altar of acacia wood overlaid with bronze in the tabernacle court; site of all burnt offerings and the principal sacrificial altar (Exod 27:1-8; 38:1-7).
webster_summary: The main sacrificial altar in the tabernacle court.
webster_full: The large square altar of acacia wood overlaid with bronze, with horns at the four corners, standing in the tabernacle court; site of all burnt offerings and the principal sacrificial altar of Israel's worship.
scriptures: Exodus 27:1-2
And thou shalt make an altar of shittim wood, five cubits long, and five cubits broad... and thou shalt make the horns of it upon the four corners thereof.
Leviticus 1:5
And he shall kill the bullock before the LORD: and the priests, Aaron's sons, shall bring the blood, and sprinkle the blood round about upon the altar.
Hebrews 13:10
We have an altar, whereof they have no right to eat which serve the tabernacle.
corruption_summary: Forgotten as obsolete furniture; missing how Hebrews names the cross as our altar.
corruption_paragraphs: The bronze altar where animal blood was shed daily prefigures the cross where Christ shed His blood once. Hebrews 13:10 declares: 'we have an altar' — but it is no longer of bronze; it is the cross of Christ.
usage: The bronze altar prefigures the cross.
We have an altar; the cross is its name.

etymology: Hebrew bamah (בָּמָה) — "raised place," hilltop or platform of worship.
biblical_def: Elevated cultic shrines on hilltops, often used for syncretistic worship after the conquest; tolerated under early Israel, condemned under Hezekiah and Josiah's reforms (1 Kings 14:23; 2 Kings 18:4; 23:8-9).
webster_summary: Hilltop shrines, often syncretistic, condemned by reformer kings.
webster_full: Elevated cultic shrines on hilltops or raised platforms, often used for syncretistic worship of YHWH mixed with Baal or Asherah; tolerated under early Israel before centralized worship in Jerusalem; systematically destroyed under Hezekiah's and Josiah's reforms.
scriptures: 1 Kings 14:23
For they also built them high places, and images, and groves, on every high hill, and under every green tree.
2 Kings 18:4
He removed the high places, and brake the images, and cut down the groves.
2 Kings 23:8
And he brought all the priests out of the cities of Judah, and defiled the high places where the priests had burned incense, from Geba to Beersheba.
corruption_summary: Forgotten archaeology; missing how it teaches the perpetual danger of mixing worship of God with worship of idols.
corruption_paragraphs: High places were not all pagan — many were sincere YHWH-worship done in the wrong place and in the wrong way. The lesson is that sincerity does not sanctify wrong worship. Centralized, regulated worship was God's command, not optional preference.
usage: Tear down the high places of your heart.
Sincere worship in wrong terms is still wrong.

etymology: Hebrew asherah (אֲשֵׁרָה) — wooden cult-symbol of the Canaanite goddess Asherah.
biblical_def: The wooden cult-symbol (often called 'grove' in KJV) of the Canaanite mother-goddess Asherah; Israel was commanded to cut them down (Exod 34:13; Deut 7:5; 16:21); the perpetual snare of the kings.
webster_summary: Wooden cult-symbol of the Canaanite goddess Asherah.
webster_full: The wooden cultic pole or carved symbol associated with the Canaanite mother-goddess Asherah, often planted near altars; commanded by the Mosaic law to be cut down and burned; tolerated under most kings of Israel and Judah, removed only under reformers.
scriptures: Exodus 34:13
But ye shall destroy their altars, break their images, and cut down their groves.
Deuteronomy 16:21
Thou shalt not plant thee a grove of any trees near unto the altar of the LORD thy God, which thou shalt make thee.
2 Kings 23:6
And he brought out the grove from the house of the LORD... and burned it at the brook Kidron, and stamped it small to powder.
corruption_summary: Hidden behind the KJV's translation 'grove' so modern readers don't realize they are reading about the goddess.
corruption_paragraphs: KJV translates asherah as 'grove' which obscures the goddess. The thing was a cult-symbol of the mother-goddess Asherah, often placed beside YHWH-altars. The lesson: idols of femininity-worship are old and persistent. Reformer kings cut them down. We should too.
usage: Cut down the asherah of the heart.
KJV's 'grove' is a goddess-symbol.

etymology: From Old English grafen "carved"; Hebrew pesel (פֶּסֶל) — carved image.
biblical_def: Any sculpted, carved, or molded representation made for worship — explicitly forbidden in the second commandment (Exod 20:4; Deut 5:8).
webster_summary: A carved or sculpted idol forbidden in the second commandment.
webster_full: Any image, sculpture, or carving made for worship — whether of a creature, a deity, or even of YHWH Himself; forbidden by the second commandment as a fundamental violation of God's spiritual nature and the unrepresentability of His glory in carved form.
scriptures: Exodus 20:4-5
Thou shalt not make unto thee any graven image, or any likeness of any thing... thou shalt not bow down thyself to them, nor serve them.
Deuteronomy 4:15-16
Take ye therefore good heed unto yourselves... lest ye corrupt yourselves, and make you a graven image.
Isaiah 44:9-10
They that make a graven image are all of them vanity... who hath formed a god, or molten a graven image that is profitable for nothing?
corruption_summary: Read as merely a prohibition of foreign idols, missing the warning against making images of YHWH Himself.
corruption_paragraphs: The second commandment forbids carved images even of YHWH. The golden calf was meant to be YHWH (Aaron 'made a feast unto the LORD'). Israel sinned by trying to picture the right God. Visual worship of God in image is the perpetual temptation.
usage: No carved image of God; He has not given His likeness.
Worship in spirit and truth.

etymology: Hebrew teraphim (תְּרָפִים) — household idols used for divination.
biblical_def: Household idols used for divination and inheritance-rights; Rachel stole her father Laban's; Michal used one to deceive Saul's messengers (Gen 31:19; 1 Sam 19:13; 2 Kings 23:24).
webster_summary: Household idols for divination.
webster_full: Household idols of varying size used in the ancient Near East for divination and to signal household leadership and inheritance rights; possessed and used at times even within Israel; condemned by the prophets and Josiah's reform.
scriptures: Genesis 31:19
And Laban went to shear his sheep: and Rachel had stolen the images that were her father's.
1 Samuel 19:13
And Michal took an image, and laid it in the bed... and covered it with a cloth.
2 Kings 23:24
Moreover the workers with familiar spirits, and the wizards, and the images, and the idols... did Josiah put away.
corruption_summary: Forgotten as ancient curio; missing how thoroughly household idolatry plagued even the patriarchal family.
corruption_paragraphs: Teraphim were household-level idolatry — kept in homes, used for guidance, signifying authority. Rachel's theft hints at Laban's lingering paganism. Israel's homes carried these images for centuries. Family idolatry is the hardest to root out.
usage: Tear teraphim from the house.
Family idolatry hides longest.

etymology: Greek phylakterion (φυλακτήριον) — "safeguard"; Hebrew tefillin — "prayers."
biblical_def: Small leather boxes containing Scripture verses (Exod 13:9; Deut 6:8; 11:18) bound on forehead and arm; commanded as memorial; criticized by Jesus when worn for show (Matt 23:5).
webster_summary: Leather scripture-boxes worn on head and arm.
webster_full: Small leather boxes containing four short Scripture passages, bound on the forehead and left arm during morning prayer; called tefillin in Hebrew; commanded in the Torah as physical memorial of God's word; criticized by Jesus when worn enlarged for ostentation.
scriptures: Deuteronomy 6:8
And thou shalt bind them for a sign upon thine hand, and they shall be as frontlets between thine eyes.
Exodus 13:9
And it shall be for a sign unto thee upon thine hand, and for a memorial between thine eyes, that the LORD's law may be in thy mouth.
Matthew 23:5
But all their works they do for to be seen of men: they make broad their phylacteries, and enlarge the borders of their garments.
corruption_summary: Read as legalism by Christians who miss the original commandment; or as religious-cosplay by those who forget the heart-warning.
corruption_paragraphs: Phylacteries are commanded; large showy phylacteries are condemned. The same word can be obedience or pride depending on the heart. Jesus does not abolish the practice; He rebukes the performance. The principle survives every external practice.
usage: Bind the Word on hand and forehead — really and metaphorically.
Beware enlarged phylacteries.

etymology: Composite term for the seven main pieces commanded in Exodus 25-30.
biblical_def: The seven main pieces of furniture in the tabernacle: bronze altar, bronze laver, golden lampstand, table of showbread, altar of incense, ark of the covenant, mercy seat — each rich in typological meaning.
webster_summary: The seven main pieces of tabernacle furniture.
webster_full: The set of furniture commanded in Exodus 25-30 for the Mosaic tabernacle: bronze altar, bronze laver, golden lampstand, table of showbread, altar of incense, ark of the covenant, mercy seat — each in a specific location and rich with typological meaning fulfilled in Christ.
scriptures: Exodus 25:8-9
And let them make me a sanctuary; that I may dwell among them. According to all that I shew thee... so shall ye make it.
Hebrews 9:2-5
There was a tabernacle made; the first... wherein was the candlestick, and the table, and the shewbread; which is called the sanctuary.
Hebrews 8:5
Who serve unto the example and shadow of heavenly things.
corruption_summary: Skimmed in modern Bible reading; missing how every furnishing is a Christ-type and how the layout itself preaches.
corruption_paragraphs: The tabernacle is a portable sermon. Every piece preaches: altar = atonement, laver = cleansing, lampstand = Spirit-illumination, showbread = Christ's body, incense = prayer, ark = throne, mercy seat = propitiation. Read Exodus 25-30 as gospel preview.
roots_summary: Hebrew kelei ha-mishkan — vessels of the dwelling.
usage: Read Exodus 25-30 as Christology.
Every furnishing preaches the gospel.
